demo.code:
import math
TITLE = 'Jasper Foundation Stone'
N = 1.52
D = 0.01
INC = 45.0
nb = N + D / 2.0
nr = N - D / 2.0
ab = math.degrees(math.asin(math.sin(math.radians(INC)) / nb))
ar = math.degrees(math.asin(math.sin(math.radians(INC)) / nr))
print(TITLE + ' - dispersion calculator')
print('Mean refractive index: %.3f, dispersion: %.3f' % (N, D))
print('Blue-side refracted angle: %.2f degrees' % ab)
print('Red-side refracted angle: %.2f degrees' % ar)
print('Angular spread: %.2f degrees' % abs(ar - ab))
demo.expected_output:

engineering_view: Engineering view: Foundation ordering in a built course follows the textual order from the lowest course upward, with each stone's course labelled by its position number so the sequence can be checked at a glance. Course heights are design choices, and the demo computes how many courses a foundation height needs at an adopted course height.

The twelve courses are numbered 1 to 12 in the Revelation 21:19-20 order: jasper, sapphire, chalcedony, emerald, sardonyx, sardius, chrysolite, beryl, topaz, chrysoprase, jacinth, amethyst. Any display or model that reorders the courses must label itself as a reordering, not as the textual order.

parameters.Order: Revelation 21:19-20, jasper first to amethyst twelfth

title: Optical Data Method
text_faithful_view: Text-faithful view (faith interpretation): No optical method is given in Revelation 21; the stones are named, not measured. Optical measurement belongs to the engineering programme.
engineering_view: Engineering view: Refractive index is measured with a refractometer on a polished flat, dispersion from indices at blue and red wavelengths, absorption with a spectroscope or spectrometer, and colour with a standard colour chart under controlled light. Each measurement is recorded with its instrument, sample, and date, so the data can be audited.
body: Signature-original design: this record approximates the corresponding public record with Signature-original materials and detailing. Where any part of it is speculative it is labelled Signature-original, and it is never presented as an authentic public record. The method order is: identify the sample, polish a flat, measure the index, measure dispersion, record the absorption spectrum in words, and photograph the colour under daylight-balanced light. A stone measured by another method must state that method, because different methods give slightly different index values.

demo.code:
import math
TITLE = 'Optical Data Method'
N = 1.6
INC = 45.0
refr = math.degrees(math.asin(math.sin(math.radians(INC)) / N))
crit = math.degrees(math.asin(1.0 / N))
print(TITLE + ' - refraction calculator')
print('Refractive index: %.2f' % N)
print('Incident angle: %.1f degrees' % INC)
print('Refracted angle: %.2f degrees' % refr)
print('Critical angle: %.2f degrees' % crit)
demo.expected_output:
Optical Data Method - refraction calculator
Refractive index: 1.60
Incident angle: 45.0 degrees
Refracted angle: 26.23 degrees
Critical angle: 38.68 degrees

title: Foundation Mounting and Structure
text_faithful_view: Text-faithful view (faith interpretation): Revelation 21:19 says the wall's foundations are adorned with precious stones, and verse 14 associates the twelve foundations with the apostles' names. The passage gives no mounting detail.
engineering_view: Engineering view: Foundation stones are mounted as facing units on a structural foundation course, set in mortar or on mechanical fixings, with each course tied back to the core. Large stones are cramped with stainless dowels, small stones are set in panels, and the whole foundation is protected from ground moisture by a damp-proof course.
body: Signature-original design: this record approximates the corresponding public record with Signature-original materials and detailing. Where any part of it is speculative it is labelled Signature-original, and it is never presented as an authentic public record. Mounting follows the same discipline as the jasper wall: units sorted by course, joints staggered, fixings tested by pull-out, and each course photographed before the next is set. A foundation course that cannot be inspected after the next course is built must be inspected before it is covered.

demo.code:
TITLE = 'Foundation Mounting and Structure'
L = 1.0
W = 0.5
H = 0.3
DENS = 2400
vol = L * W * H
mass = vol * DENS
print(TITLE + ' - block mass calculator')
print('Block: %.2f m x %.2f m x %.2f m' % (L, W, H))
print('Volume: %.2f cubic metres' % vol)
print('Density: %.0f kg per cubic metre' % DENS)
print('Mass: %.0f kg' % mass)
demo.expected_output:
Foundation Mounting and Structure - block mass calculator
Block: 1.00 m x 0.50 m x 0.30 m
Volume: 0.15 cubic metres
Density: 2400 kg per cubic metre
Mass: 360 kg

title: Alternative Foundation Mappings
text_faithful_view: Text-faithful view (faith interpretation): The ancient stone names in Revelation 21:19-20 do not map one-to-one onto modern minerals with certainty, and scholars differ on several stones, notably chrysolite, jacinth, and sardius. The passage does not resolve those differences.
engineering_view: Engineering view: This record keeps the main mapping and its alternatives in one table so no reader mistakes a scholarly reading for a settled fact. The demo compares refraction for two candidate indices for the most disputed stone in the set, jacinth, showing how much the optics change if the alternative identification is adopted.
body: Signature-original design: this record approximates the corresponding public record with Signature-original materials and detailing. Where any part of it is speculative it is labelled Signature-original, and it is never presented as an authentic public record. The rule for the whole pair is: every stone record carries its alternative identification, every summary that lists stones carries a note that identifications are readings, and no design calculation uses an alternative index without saying so. Where a mapping is widely agreed, the record says so; where it is disputed, the record says that too.
